title: "Data-Manager Identity and Tracking"
date: 2026-10-12

**Status (2026-10-19): Design guide, revised. Container runs already take the
syphilis release declared in committed code; Phases A–E below are planned, and
Phase A is next.** Requested by the team on 2026-10-09: make specifications,
likelihoods, calibrations, and saved simulation sets aware of which data managers
(name and version) they used, including several managers at once and different
releases at different points of a process. This page fixes the target design,
its phases, and their acceptance criteria, so the work stays consistent across
sessions.

**Revision (2026-10-19).** The first version (2026-10-12) put selection last and
proposed recording exact reads first. This revision puts selection first, since it
determines which data a run uses and is the part the team works with directly. It
records complete-but-conservative context before exact reads, because a partial
trace of reads can name the wrong dependency ([recording](#recording)). It also
adds how releases are chosen in each application today and the hazards found. The
delivery practice is [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028).

**Verified against:** jheem2 `dev`
[`85b73171`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/tree/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e),
jheem_analyses
[`eb991798`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/tree/eb991798),
jheem-containers
[`39649e9f`](https://github.com/ncsizemore/jheem-containers/tree/39649e9f50e20ff25adc53b691fdf61bbd7266cd),
and bayesian.simulations `4e0d13e8`. Measurements are from shield2 on 2026-10-09.

**Candidate durable home:** the engine contract (identity, registry, records,
comparison) in jheem2 documentation; declarations, loading, and the release store
in the jheem_analyses and jheem-containers READMEs. **Graduation:** when Phase D
ships, this page shrinks to a summary with links.

Related: [reproducibility contract](reproducibility.qmd),
[manager selection and compatibility](manager-compatibility.qmd),
[SHIELD container pilot](shield-container-pilot.qmd#current-installation),
[D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027), and [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028).

## Goal {#goal}

The work is complete when these hold:

- **R1 Select.** A run's managers are immutable releases declared in its
  committed analysis code, loaded once and verified, so code and data move together
  and container and native runs of one commit use the same data
  ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)).
- **R2 Identify.** A manager's identity is its content (a digest of the loaded
  file), with the release tag as a label when known. A manager changed in memory
  after loading is marked as changed.
- **R3 Record.** Every artifact whose numbers depend on manager data records which
  manager releases it depended on, stating how complete that record is: kernels
  (and so every simulation set), instantiated likelihoods, and calibrations.
- **R4 Check.** Deriving something new from an artifact (rerunning its
  simulations, transmuting it, or starting the next calibration stage) compares the
  managers in memory with the recorded ones and reports differences.
- **R5 No behavior change** until a phase deliberately introduces one: numeric
  outputs are unchanged, analysts take no new steps, and artifacts saved before the
  change still load and run.
- **R6 Several managers.** Everything is kept per named manager, so a run that
  uses census and surveillance managers, or different releases at different
  stages, is selected, recorded, and checked for each.

Not in scope: changing scientific code or likelihood definitions; requiring the
existing references to manager globals to change; a general artifact registry;
stopping runs on a mismatch by default.

## How data reaches results today {#binding-points}

| When data is read | Example | Where the result is kept | Release recorded? |
|---|---|---|---|
| While analysis code is sourced | SHIELD likelihood instructions read national 1970–1993 totals ([`shield_likelihoods.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/shield_likelihoods.R#L229)) | In-memory instructions | No |
| Kernel construction | `create.jheem.kernel()` evaluates each element's value or functional-form function ([`JHEEM_kernel.R:156-160`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_kernel.R#L156-L160), [`SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R:5042-5108`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/SPECIFICATION_model_specification.R#L5042-L5108)). SHIELD registers 26 such functions; they read the `CENSUS.MANAGER` and `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` globals. Kernels are rebuilt on every call. | The kernel, saved inside every simulation set | No |
| Likelihood instantiation | Observations are pulled from the manager passed in ([`LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R:929`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/LIKELIHOODS_basic_likelihood.R#L929)); outcome-location mappings read the default manager ([`JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R:143`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_outcome_location_mappings.R#L143)) | The instantiated likelihood, saved in the calibration's control file | Indirectly (below) |
| Calibration registration and setup | `register.calibration.info()` keeps a reference to a manager object, by default the default manager ([`CALIBRATION_main.R:1576`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/CALIBRATION_main.R#L1576)), when the registration file is sourced; setup later instantiates the likelihood from that object (line 488) | The likelihood closure serializes the calibration settings, including the whole manager (line 608) | Only through the loader's attribute on the embedded manager |
| Deriving from saved artifacts | `rerun.simulations()` builds a new kernel from the managers in memory ([`JHEEM_simulation.R:119`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_simulation.R#L119)); transmutation builds a kernel for the target version ([`JHEEM_transmutation.R:326`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/JHEEM_transmutation.R#L326)). Interventions reuse the saved kernel (`JHEEM_simulation.R:2302`), but runtime quantity functions can still read globals. | Nothing; whatever is in memory is used | No |
| Analysis | Plots and analysis-time likelihoods read the default manager | Not kept | No |

jheem2 itself knows two things about managers: an object passed to it, and a single
default. The names `CENSUS.MANAGER` and `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` are variables the
analysis code agrees on, not names jheem2 can resolve.

### How releases are chosen today {#selection-today}

| Application | Manager | Release chosen by | Manager already in memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| SHIELD, native | Syphilis | `SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG` in [`shield_source_code.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/eb991798/applications/SHIELD/shield_source_code.R#L44) | Reused, with a warning that the declaration was ignored |
| SHIELD, native | Census | Not declared: the release the shared cached-metadata file names | Reused silently |
| SHIELD, container | Syphilis, census | The declaration in the captured source; the installation's census | Never (each run is a new process) |
| EHE and HIV ([`source_code.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/eb991798/source_code.R#L26-L40)) | HIV surveillance, census | Not declared: the promoted release, and the cached-metadata census, at load time | Reused silently |
| Ryan White | Ryan White managers | A file path in the local cache; no version | Not applicable |

Only one manager across these applications is selected by an explicit version.
Nothing records what the others resolved to.

### Hazards found {#hazards}

- **No content identity.** The manager object holds a name (for example
  `syphilis.manager_section3`, a build label), a description, timestamps, and a code
  iteration. Eight methods change it in place
  ([`DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R`](https://github.com/CIPHER-Epi/jheem2/blob/85b731715bf3eaf81021141b142ebdf53230707e/R/DATA_MANAGER_data_manager.R#L618)).
  The analyses loader attaches the release tag and SHA-256 as an R attribute, which
  jheem2 never reads.
- **One variable name, two managers.** `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` is the syphilis
  manager in SHIELD and the HIV manager in EHE, and both loaders skip loading when the
  variable already exists. By code reading, a session that sources EHE's setup and
  then SHIELD's would run SHIELD on the HIV manager, with only a warning. This has
  not been observed.
- **Selection at the wrong time.** Calibration registrations capture a manager
  object when the registration file is sourced, not when the calibration starts.
- **Timestamps as versions.** Two SHIELD helpers branch on
  `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER$last.modified.date >= 2026-08-01`
  ([`shield_specification_helpers.R`](https://github.com/tfojo1/jheem_analyses/blob/08a250c347eb50b24907c091f6fdbdadb93c70d6/applications/SHIELD/R/shield_specification_helpers.R#L138)).
- **Managers built from other managers.** The syphilis manager carries its own
  census-derived population (source `census.aggregated.population`). Its build takes
  census from the dependency bundle `data-managers-latest`, which holds the census
  last modified 2025-04-23, while SHIELD kernels use the census of 2026-10-08. The
  population a likelihood compares against may therefore come from a different
  census build than the population the model simulates. This is inferred from the
  sources and build records, not measured.
- **Scale.** jheem_analyses has 845 references to `CENSUS.MANAGER` or
  `SURVEILLANCE.MANAGER` in 85 R files; 32 jheem2 function signatures default to
  `get.default.data.manager()`.
- **Embedded manager, missing census.** For one SHIELD stage-0 city, the
  calibration's `global_control.Rdata` was 132.7 MB on disk and holds the whole
  syphilis manager: 2,471.5 MB serialized, against 0.8 MB for the calibration settings
  without it. Loading it took 9.5 s and about 2.9 GB of memory. The census manager is
  recorded nowhere.
- **Releases change mid-pipeline unnoticed.** One city's native pipeline ran stages
  0–1 before the syphilis release of 2026-10-09 existed and stages 2–3 with it; only
  log lines show it.

## Design principles {#principles}

1. **Data is an input, like code** ([D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027)): selected per
   run, frozen within it, and recorded, not built into a runtime.
2. **Select explicitly, then record and check.** Selection decides which data a run
   uses; records and checks report what happened.
3. **Identity is content; tags are labels.**
4. **A record states its coverage.** A conservative record that may list too much is
   acceptable; a record that claims to be exact and can miss a dependency is not.
5. **Additive and backward compatible.** Saved kernels, likelihoods, and simulation
   metadata are non-portable R6 objects that carry their own methods, so objects
   saved earlier never gain new methods. New information lives in private fields
   read through package-level functions that treat a missing field as "not
   recorded".
6. **Behavior changes are explicit.** They arrive behind an option that is off by
   default, then are switched on deliberately ([D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028)).

## Design {#design}

### 1. Identity on the manager (Phase A, jheem2) {#identity}

A private field holds a provenance record, read through
`get.data.manager.provenance(manager)`:

| Field | Set by | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `file` | `load.data.manager()` | Base name of the loaded file |
| `md5` | `load.data.manager()`, using `tools::md5sum` from base R | Content identity, available for every loaded manager |
| `sha256`, `release`, `repository` | The caller, through a new optional `provenance` argument to `load.data.manager()`; the analyses loader passes its verified resolution | Release identity, when known |
| `loaded.at` | `load.data.manager()` | Load time |
| `modified` | `FALSE` at load; `TRUE` after any of the eight methods that change contents | The identity no longer describes the contents |

`load.data.manager()` already copies a saved manager through the current class
constructor, so every newly loaded manager carries the field. jheem2 imports no
hashing package; MD5 identifies content here, while integrity checks of releases
keep using SHA-256 in the loader and the store. Copies inherit the source's record;
managers created in memory have no file or digest. Two records match when their
SHA-256 (or, failing that, MD5) agree and neither is modified.

### 2. Named registry (Phase A, jheem2) {#registry}

- `register.data.manager(name, manager)` returns the manager, so a setup line can
  keep its global: `CENSUS.MANAGER <- register.data.manager("census", ...)`.
- `get.data.manager(name)` returns it, or stops with a message naming the missing
  manager. `list.data.managers()` lists names with their provenance.
- The default manager is unchanged. Nothing in jheem2 consults the registry until a
  later phase opts in.

### 3. Selection (Phase B, jheem_analyses and jheem-containers) {#selection}

Four steps, each small:

1. **Declare.** Each application keeps one list of the managers it uses, in
   committed code, replacing `SYPHILIS.MANAGER.RELEASE.TAG`:
   ```r
   SHIELD.DATA.MANAGERS <- list(
       census   = list(file = "census.manager.rdata",   release = "census-manager-v2026.10.08"),
       syphilis = list(file = "syphilis.manager.rdata", release = "syphilis-manager-v2026.10.09"))
   ```
   The names are what code refers to; the releases are the versions. A version
   change is a reviewable commit.
2. **Resolve and load once.** The application's setup loads each declared release
   through the verified loader, passes its identity to jheem2, registers it under its
   name, and assigns the existing globals. A manager already in memory is reused only
   if its identity matches the declaration; otherwise it is reloaded.
3. **Override, recorded.** An explicit run-time override (for example
   `JHEEM_DATA_OVERRIDES="census=census-manager-v2026.10.20"`) for experiments,
   stated in the run's record, so nobody edits the declaration to try something.
4. **Freeze.** The resolved selection (name, release, digest) is saved with the run;
   continuations and later stages reuse it unless a later stage deliberately selects
   anew (see [decisions](#decisions)).

**How existing code is affected.** Specification helpers keep reading the globals,
which now hold the declared releases. A helper may switch from
`CENSUS.MANAGER$pull(...)` to `get.data.manager("census")$pull(...)` at any time; a
specification may declare the names it needs so kernel construction checks them up
front. Calibration registrations may name their manager
(`data.manager = "syphilis"`), resolved when setup runs rather than when the
registration file is sourced; passing an object keeps working. None of these
changes is required.

**Containers** read the same list from the captured source instead of the single
syphilis line, so census follows committed code too. That requires census to have
dated, immutable releases (`census-manager-v2026.10.08` exists) and a publishing path
for later census updates.

### 4. Recording (Phase C, jheem2) {#recording}

Records are stored on artifacts in private fields, read with `get.data.inputs(x)`
for a kernel, simulation set, likelihood, or calibration directory (`NULL` for
artifacts saved earlier). Calibration setup also writes a readable
`data_inputs.dcf` in the calibration directory. Each record states its coverage:

| Coverage | Meaning | Phase |
|---|---|---|
| `declared` | The selection the run made (names, releases, digests) | C1 |
| `loaded` | Every manager registered or loaded in the session when the artifact was built | C1 |
| `read` | Managers observed being read while the artifact was built | C2 |
| `unknown` | The artifact predates recording, or a manager has no identity | Any |

C1 is complete but conservative: a dependency read while sourcing, before any
artifact existed, is still covered by `loaded`. C2 adds a private `note.read()` in
each read method and active binding of the manager class, and capture scopes around
kernel construction, likelihood instantiation, and calibration setup. Observed reads
can miss values computed earlier (for example, likelihood instructions computed
from release A before release B is loaded), so C2 never replaces C1. It must pass a
test of that exact case.

Container runs already record census and syphilis tags and digests in
`inputs.json`; the jheem2 records link to that run history rather than defining a
second one.

### 5. Checking (Phase D, jheem2) {#detection}

- `compare.data.inputs(recorded, current)` reports, per name, a changed release, a
  manager changed in memory, or a manager missing on either side.
- Option `jheem2.data.change`: `"ignore"` when first shipped, then `"warn"`;
  `"stop"` on request.
- **Checked when:**
  - `rerun.simulations()` builds a new kernel;
  - `set.up.calibration()` has preceding codes, against the preceding calibration's
    record (this would have flagged the mixed-release pipeline at stage 2);
  - transmutation, for managers shared by parent and target;
  - optionally, analysis-time likelihood instantiation.
- A deliberate change proceeds and is recorded with the parent's inputs.

### 6. Beyond SHIELD (Phase E) {#beyond-shield}

- EHE and HIV declare their managers under distinct names (for example
  `hiv.surveillance`), retiring the ambiguous shared variable name.
- Ryan White managers get dated releases.
- Native loading prefers the shared release store over personal cached copies.
- Manager builds record the identities of the managers they consume, so the
  census-inside-syphilis case becomes visible.
- Decide when calibration controls stop embedding the manager.

### Manager embedded in calibration controls {#embedded-manager}

Keep it for now: for managers without retained immutable releases, it is the only
kept copy of the data a calibration used. Once every manager a calibration uses is a
retained release, setup can record identities instead and drop about 2.5 GB of
serialized manager from each control (132.7 MB on disk per city and stage, 9.5 s and
2.9 GB of memory at each chain start).

## Phases {#phases}

| Phase | Scope | Repositories | Acceptance | State (2026-10-19) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Container runs take the syphilis release declared in committed code; shared verified store | jheem-containers, jheem_analyses | [D-027](../decisions.qmd#d-027); installation accepted | Shipped for container runs |
| A | jheem2 test gate; manager identity; named registry; loader passes identity | jheem2, jheem-containers, jheem_analyses | Gates below; no output or behavior change | Next |
| B | Declared list per application (SHIELD first); resolve, verify, register, freeze; recorded overrides; containers read the list; census release path | jheem_analyses, jheem-containers | Native and container runs of one commit load identical releases for every SHIELD manager; an already-loaded manager with the wrong identity is reloaded | Planned |
| C1 | `declared` and `loaded` records on kernels, likelihoods, calibrations, linked to run history | jheem2, jheem_analyses | New artifacts name every SHIELD manager with its digest; earlier artifacts load and run | Planned |
| D | Comparison and checks at rerun, next stage, transmutation; option off, then warn | jheem2 | A rerun after a census change, and a stage whose syphilis release differs from its predecessor's, are reported by name | Planned |
| C2 | Observed reads with capture scopes | jheem2 | The A-then-B test passes; no record claims `read` coverage it lacks | Planned |
| E | Beyond SHIELD (above) | All | Every application's managers are declared and recorded | Planned |

### Phase A gates {#gates}

- **Tests run in the jheem-containers CI**, which already builds jheem2 at a chosen
  commit ([D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028)). A small test file in jheem2 uses the
  [toy fixture](../toy-fixture-spike.qmd) and a tiny data manager to check:
  - identity at load, the modified flag, and copies;
  - registry behavior and its error messages;
  - records surviving saving and loading;
  - objects without the new fields still working.
- **No numeric change:**
  - SHIELD kernel inputs for the 26 configured cities that build are identical
    before and after, using the comparison method of 2026-10-09;
  - a short container calibration is bit-identical to one without the change.
- **No behavior change:** the same launchers run unchanged, and nothing new is
  printed.

## Delivery practice {#delivery}

Adopted as [D-028](../decisions.qmd#d-028):

- Work happens on short-lived branches and merges to jheem2 `dev` only after its
  gates pass; the team loads jheem2 from `dev` source, so a merge reaches every new
  session at once.
- Additive phases (A, C1, C2) merge when ready.
- Behavior changes (selection's reload rule, Phase D's checks) merge with an option
  that defaults to today's behavior, and are switched on in a separate, announced
  change. This avoids long-lived branches drifting from `dev` while the team keeps
  committing.
- New engine code goes in its own file (for example
  `R/DATA_MANAGER_provenance.R`), with small hooks in existing files.

## Rollout and risks {#rollout}

- **Cost.** One extra read of each loaded manager file to hash it (about 100 MB for
  census or syphilis); a few hundred bytes per recorded artifact.
- **Compatibility.** Objects saved before a phase keep their old methods and lack
  the new fields; the package-level accessors return `NULL` for them.
- **Analysis code.** Moving helpers from globals to names, and replacing the two
  timestamp checks, remain the analysts' choice; the design does not depend on them.
- **Operator guides** explain warnings when Phase D switches them on.

## Decisions to finalize before Phase B {#decisions}

Proposed defaults, to confirm before Phase B starts:

1. **Where declarations live:** one list per application (proposed), rather than per
   calibration code.
2. **Stages and newer data:** a pipeline keeps its selection; a later stage may
   select newer data only through a new calibration code, which records the change
   (proposed).
3. **Names:** one per manager kind (`census`, `syphilis`, `hiv.surveillance`, ...)
   (proposed).
4. **Census releases:** dated releases published from each census update; until
   census manager CI exists, a small publishing script run when the cached-metadata
   file changes (proposed).
5. **The default manager:** kept, set from a named manager, for plotting and
   analysis (proposed).

## Open questions {#open-questions}

1. Hashing in jheem2: base-R MD5 plus loader-supplied SHA-256 (proposed), or a new
   hashing dependency.
2. Whether the cross-manager census difference is material: compare the syphilis
   manager's census-derived population with the census manager's, for the ten
   SHIELD cities.
3. When calibration controls stop embedding the manager.
4. Store-first loading for native runs.
